title: LLM command envelope (schema_version 1.0 / 1.1)
description: The exactly-5-field envelope an LLM/agent process sends as the ubus call argument to `router_display`'s `llm_command` method. This is also the argument object itself, not a nested/escaped JSON string. See Router_App/router_display_src/LLM_JSON_CMD.md for the prose spec and docs/llm_integration_ubus.md for the transport (ubus object/method/ack/event).

schema_version.description: Contract version. "1.0" = the base commands. "1.1" (since 2026-10-07) = 1.0 plus `arguments.schedule` on block / unblock / set_guest_wifi and the schedule commands (`cancel_schedule`, get_info `query:schedule_list`). Any other value is rejected with ack error 'Invalid command envelope'. A 1.0 envelope carrying a schedule is refused during execution ('schedule requires schema_version 1.1'). `router_display status` lists both under `schema_versions`.

request_id.description: Monotonic per-caller sequence number, starting at 1. Must be a JSON integer, not a numeric string — a string value is rejected with ack error 'request_id must be a positive integer'. Sequence is tracked per ubus caller connection (peer), not globally.

command.description: `cancel_schedule` needs schema_version 1.1 and target {"type":"schedules"}. Any value outside this set is rejected with ack error 'Unknown command'. The last two are ACCEPTED BUT NOT ACTED ON: `open_qos` and `device_control` are in llm_dispatch.c's s_llm_commands_planned[], so the ack says accepted:true and execution answers ok:false 'Not implemented yet: ...' to the LCD panel/syslog only. They are in the enum because a caller emitting them is not making a schema error - it is exercising a command whose implementation is pending. Read `commands` vs `commands_planned` from `router_display status` to tell the two groups apart at runtime. `show_intro` (2026-11-13) is UI only: target gateway, `arguments.topic` product|wifi8|vnpt; the panel opens that intro chapter (docs/json_command_protocol.md section 4.2). `set_language` (2026-11-13) is UI only too: target gateway, `arguments.language` en|vi (absolute, never a toggle); the panel and the web engine switch their UI language and, through the audio frames' LANG byte, the STT language (docs/json_command_protocol.md section 4.3).

arguments.description: Command-specific arguments. Exact shape depends on `command` — see the per-command $defs below and Router_App/router_display_src/LLM_JSON_CMD.md §4-5.

selector.description: Either a MAC address the caller resolved itself from router_snapshot.yaml (six hex pairs, ':' or '-', any case -- what the router agent sends for every device write since 2026-10-07), or a raw device NAME taken from the user's utterance, e.g. "SON", "con", "iPad cua me". A MAC-shaped selector is matched exactly against the client table and never falls through to the name stages. A name is resolved daemon-side -- exact name, then substring name. Both stages fold case AND Vietnamese diacritics before comparing (vn_fold() in llm_dispatch.c), so an accented selector matches a client whose DHCP hostname is unaccented ("Quoc"), in either case, and decomposed (NFD) input folds the same as precomposed. minLength stays 1 because a 1-character exact name is still resolvable, but the daemon's substring stage requires at least 3 characters (UTF-8 characters, not bytes: "bo" with a Vietnamese tone mark is 2 characters / 4 bytes and is below the floor). Ambiguous or unresolvable selectors are not rejected at the ack stage -- the failure is written only to the LCD panel/syslog and never reaches the LLM caller (see docs/llm_integration_ubus.md).

target_devices.description: Plural gateway-wide scope, accepted by `get_info` with query=online_clients (or its `filter: "online"` spelling) as an alias for target_gateway. No other command accepts it: llm_expected_target() in llm_dispatch.c pins every other command to gateway or device, and this alias is checked only inside the online_clients branch.

args_get_info.description: Either a `query` (the normal form) or the `filter: "online"` alias, which llm_cmd_get_info() resolves to query=online_clients before dispatching. Send exactly one of the two.

application.description: Which AI QoS traffic class to list, for query=active_application_sessions ONLY - required there, meaningless elsewhere. The four a person actually asks about are GAMING, VSTREAM, VOICE and VIDEOCALL; BACKGROUND is accepted by the same code path. The daemon resolves the name with sec_qos_tc_from_name(), the same resolver the feed parser uses, so common variants (VIDEO_STREAM, VOIP, GAME, ...) also work - the enum here is the canonical set the LLM should emit, which is why it is not `additionalProperties: false` territory. An unknown name is a result failure (`Unknown application '<x>'`), not an ack rejection.

query.description: Target type depends on the query: gateway for connection_quality / router_status / online_clients / active_application_sessions, device for client_detail (online_clients and active_application_sessions also accept target_devices). That dependency is why llm_validate() cannot check it and a mismatch surfaces as a result msg instead of an ack error. `router_status` returns the router's own health (sys/board, same field names as the periodic stats packet) and makes the panel open its System Monitor screen. `active_application_sessions` lists the devices the other team's AI QoS feed put one traffic class on, selected by `arguments.application` (required); with the feed unreadable it answers ok:false 'AI QoS feed unavailable' rather than an empty list, because empty would assert something never observed. `active_gaming_sessions` is the RETIRED spelling of that query fixed to application=GAMING - still accepted so an un-updated prompt keeps working, but new callers should send active_application_sessions. Every get_info answer reaches only the LCD panel/syslog, never the LLM (see docs/llm_integration_ubus.md).

args_block.description: An empty object is valid and is the common case: `scope` is OPTIONAL and defaults to "internet" (llm_scope_is_internet() in llm_dispatch.c), because a spoken "block Nam's internet" carries no scope of its own. Any other `scope` spelling (without `application`) is refused during execution.

scope.description: Omit it for the whole-device internet block. "application" is equivalent to sending `application`.

application.description: WIDENED TO THE WHOLE DEVICE (product decision 2026-10-07). There is no per-application rule (the firewall rules are per-MAC, no DPI), so a request naming an application (e.g. "GAMING") blocks the device's whole Internet. The result says so: msg suffix '(whole device: per-application <app> not supported)', data.requested_application and data.applied_to:"device", and a syslog 'degraded' line.

args_unblock.description: Mirror of args_block: `scope` optional, defaults to "internet"; `application` is widened to the whole device the same way.

application.description: Widened to the whole device, named in the result exactly as for block.

priority.description: OPTIONAL, defaults to "high" (the router agent's qos.prioritize sends only `application`). Any other value is refused during execution.

scope.description: Accepted syntactically (e.g. "gaming") but currently ignored entirely by the daemon — present for forward compatibility with LLM_JSON_CMD.md §5.7's examples, has no effect on today's firmware. NOTE this is NOT the same as `application` below: scope stays silently ignored, application is recognised and refused.

application.description: WIDENED TO THE WHOLE DEVICE (product decision 2026-10-07): LLM_EXEC_OPTIMIZE builds a per-MAC QoS class covering ALL of that device's traffic. The result names the widening exactly as for block.

args_limit.description: At least one direction. A direction left out KEEPS the device's current limit in that direction (persisted policy, or the demo world's), or stays unlimited when there is none. Neither present -> ok:false 'Invalid bandwidth limits' during execution.

download_limit_mbps.description: jint_required() in llm_dispatch.c requires a JSON integer -- a decimal like 12.5 is rejected during execution (ok:false, msg:'Invalid bandwidth limits' written only to the LCD panel/syslog), not in the ack -- the LLM caller is never told. Upper bound is LLM_MAX_LIMIT_MBPS = 10000; the same message covers both the range check and the type check.

args_set_guest_wifi.description: Two accepted shapes: a boolean `enabled` (LLM_JSON_CMD.md §5.9), or a string `action` (used by the legacy test scripts). Send exactly one of the two, not both.

args_open_qos.description: ACCEPTED BUT NOT IMPLEMENTED. Opening a screen is a display command, and the panel has no QoS screen yet (action_forward_qos() in esp32/main/ui_controller/actions.c is an empty body), so the daemon answers ok:false 'Not implemented yet: open_qos screen navigation'. Both fields are hints for the eventual implementation and are not read today.

args_device_control.description: ACCEPTED BUT NOT IMPLEMENTED. Controlling a smart plug or lamp needs a home-automation bridge router_display does not talk to; it answers ok:false 'Not implemented yet: external device control'. Note target.selector here names an APPLIANCE, not a Wi-Fi client - whatever implements this must not resolve it against the DHCP client table.

target_schedules.description: The schedule table (schema 1.1): required by cancel_schedule (checked in the ack) and used by get_info query=schedule_list (gateway is accepted there too).

schedule.description: Relative or clock-time schedule (llm_schedule.c; docs/wallclock_schedules_timezone.md; LLM_JSON_CMD.md 5.12). Allowed on block, unblock, set_guest_wifi, limit, optimize. RELATIVE: {duration_minutes} act now, restore after N min; {after_minutes} act after M and keep; both = act after M, restore after N. Monotonic clock, RAM only (persistent:false). CLOCK TIME, in the router's own timezone (sys.tz), persisted to flash and reloaded at boot (persistent:true): start_time HH:MM with exactly one anchor of day (today|tomorrow), date (YYYY-MM-DD, 2000..2099) or recurrence (daily|weekdays|weekends); optional end_time (a window may cross midnight) OR duration_minutes. Refused by name, never run immediately instead: start_time with after_minutes, end_time with duration_minutes, end_time/day/date/recurrence without start_time, a router clock that is not set ('Router clock not set; clock-time schedules unavailable'), a single start already past ('Start time has already passed'). A window already in progress starts now. 'Restore' happens only while the state is still the one the schedule set - a person who changed it in between wins; for limit/optimize the state is the device's QoS policy. At most 8 live schedules. Guest Wi-Fi and QoS schedules are refused in demo mode.

schedule_id.description: Id from a 'Scheduled ...' result (data.schedule.schedule_id) or from schedule_list. A pending schedule is dropped; an active one ends now and its restore runs. Unknown id -> ok:false 'Schedule N not found'.

selectors.description: Response-latency plan 2026-11-10 L3: the devices of one person ("chặn mạng của con"), each a MAC the caller resolved; block / unblock only, never with a schedule. router_display writes them in one commit, reloads the firewall once and answers one llm_result with a row per device (data.devices[]: selector, client_name, mac, status ok | unverified | failed).

topic.description: Which showcase chapter the panel opens: the product itself, Wi-Fi 8, or VNPT.

language.description: The UI (and STT) language to switch to.
